summary.text: Bartholomew Kightley describes a 1574 Exchequer dispute involving Lady Joan Laxton and a GBP 500 debt owed by the late Francis Kightley. The deposition focuses on forbearance of the debt, new bonds, payments, damask, velvet, and a payment to Laxton's servant Edmonde.

events.label: Deposition Taken
events.description: John Birche takes the deposition of Bartholomew Kightley in the Court of Exchequer.

events.label: Loan / Debt of GBP 500
events.description: Francis Kightley is described as owing Lady Laxton GBP 500, borrowed for the old Lord Marquess of Winchester.

events.label: Request and Agreement for Forbearance
events.description: Kightley, Beswicke, and Thomson ask Lady Laxton to forbear the debt until 22 December; she agrees.

events.label: New Bonds for Assurance
events.description: New bonds are entered to assure payment of the GBP 500.

events.label: Payment for Forbearance
events.description: Twenty-five pounds is paid to Lady Laxton for forbearance of the debt.

events.label: Delivery of Damask
events.description: Damask is demanded and delivered to Lady Laxton.

events.label: Payment Toward Velvet
events.description: Fifty shillings is paid toward velvet to guard Lady Laxton's gown.

events.label: Payment to Edmonde
events.description: Twenty shillings is given to Edmonde for travel and friendship with Lady Laxton.
